First release: a facial expression classifier, from the raw FER-2013 CSV to a model you can try in a browser tab.

**Try it:** https://miguelmochizuki.github.io/fer-2013/ (nothing is uploaded; the model runs in your browser)

## What is in it

- **Training pipeline.** ResNet18 fine-tuned on FER-2013 with a weighted sampler and loss, early stopping on validation macro-F1, evaluation, Grad-CAM++ and temperature-scaling calibration.
- **API.** FastAPI on ONNX Runtime, no PyTorch in the image. YuNet finds the faces, the classifier labels each one, and `explain=true` returns the Grad-CAM++ heatmap.
- **Browser demo.** The same pipeline in JavaScript on GitHub Pages. Every stage is tested against golden files written by the Python code.

## Numbers

| | |
|---|---|
| Test accuracy / macro-F1 | 0.707 / 0.709 |
| Test ECE | 0.168 before calibration, 0.022 after (T = 2.40) |
| ONNX vs PyTorch, full test set | 70.80% vs 70.74%, 99.94% identical predictions |
| Browser, one face (Chromium) | about 115 ms end to end |
| API p50, one face | 23 ms (26 ms with the heatmap) |

## Model weights

The weights are published separately as pre-releases tagged `models-v*` ([models-v1.1.0](https://github.com/MiguelMochizuki/fer-2013/releases/tag/models-v1.1.0) is the one this release uses). They are pre-releases on purpose: the Dockerfile, CI and the site build download from them, so they must stay.

## Known limits

- About 71% accuracy on a noisy dataset. Emotion labels read off a face are not a reliable read of how someone feels; do not use this for decisions about people.
- Confidences move by several points with a few pixels of crop.
- The browser demo is checked in Chromium. Firefox and Safari are untested.
- No hosted API: the API runs anywhere Docker does, and the public demo is the browser build.
